summary:
journey with Eva: walking through time, is a project that lets you explore the rovers left behind on other worlds, through a sci-fi-inspired theory in which all of space and time becomes physical. This realm, called the Bulk, is the space you travel through as you visit each rover. Think of it as your own functional time machine, with two companions by your side: Wally and Eva.

Wally is your guide through the Bulk. He helps you understand how to navigate it.
Eva is your personal storyteller. She takes you through a world of wonders, helps you understand how the machines work, and answers any question you can think of about them.
What the Project Covers

The journey includes 9 machines left behind on two worlds:

On the Moon (4 machines): Luna 9, Apollo 11, Surveyor 3, and Lunokhod 1.
On Mars (5 machines): Viking 1, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, and Pathfinder.

We created this interactive platform to capture the attention of space and science enthusiasts. Instead of reading dull, static articles, you get to travel through a journey and learn about these abandoned rovers in an unforgettable way.

Why It Matters?

The project explores the rovers that were sent to the Moon and Mars and what they contributed to human knowledge of space. It also highlights the millions of dollars and the years of dedicated research that went into developing such wonders.
details:
People looking to learn about past space missions often work through dense technical websites or historical textbooks that lack the spark of imagination and storytelling needed to capture a younger or more casual audience's attention. To solve this, our project delivers an immersive storytelling experience that revisits historical and legacy robotic missions on the Moon and Mars. The core objective is to ensure these foundational machines are not forgotten in favor of modern tech, as they served as the essential building blocks and structural backbone for all subsequent space exploration. Later missions directly benefited from their structural designs, landing mechanisms, and site discoveries.

To make this engaging rather than a dry text format, we integrated a creative 5th dimension (5D) concept. Upon entering the web platform, users are warmly greeted by our custom chatbot, WALL-E, who acts as the cosmic guide and offers users a choice to explore either the Moon or Mars. Once a destination is selected, users transition through a cinematic journey via a black hole into the 5D space.

Upon arrival, users land on a fully immersive, 3D-modeled surface of the chosen celestial body. As they navigate the terrain, Eva—our custom Large Language Model (LLM)—dynamically appears to introduce the historical machines and rovers. Eva provides detailed insights into each machine, including its precise coordinates, scientific mission objectives, structural design, and historical significance.

Controls & Navigation: To make the 3D exploration fully interactive, users navigate the environment using WSAD keys for movement. Users can sprint or move faster by holding down the Shift key. Additionally, users can toggle the mouse cursor on or off instantly by pressing Escape to show the cursor, or simply clicking back anywhere on the screen to lock/hide it and continue immersive exploration.

System Requirements & Performance Note: Because the project features real-time 3D environments, textures, and interactive models, it requires a dedicated, capable graphics processing unit (GPU) to run smoothly. Consequently, it may experience performance limitations on laptops or devices with weaker or integrated GPUs.

Tools & Technologies: We utilized Claude and Gemini, developed our custom LLM (Eva) and interactive chatbot (WALL-E), built 3D model frameworks, and integrated official, verified datasets and resources provided by NASA.

Team Considerations & Creativity: Our team focused on delivering a uniquely captivating experience while maintaining absolute integrity regarding the effort we put in. We deliberately avoided common, overdone tropes. We chose this direction because human curiosity and the instinct to explore are timeless, and our project speaks directly to that inherent human nature.

The Use of Super Intelligence (SI) *

Super Intelligence (SI) and advanced AI tools were deeply and effectively integrated into our project's core architecture. Beyond leveraging Claude and Gemini for narrative structuring, technical ideation, and generating 3D model concepts/structures, we actively designed and implemented our custom Large Language Model (Eva) and an interactive chatbot (WALL-E) to power the project's core communication and guiding layer. We did not use AI-generated images; instead, we relied on custom AI text frameworks, model training/prompting, and 3D modeling to bring our 5D storytelling vision to life. All data and insights used strictly adhere to official NASA mission records and resources.
